newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Relief craft to Mir to be launched July 4 or 5.
newsitem.headline: Relief craft to Mir to be launched July 4 or 5.

text.p: An unmanned Progress cargo craft carrying vital repair supplies to the damaged Mir space station will be launched on July 4 or, at the latest, July 5, Russian Space Agency head Yuri Koptev said on Friday.

He told reporters at Korolyov mission control centre near Moscow that special equipment allowing the three-man Russian-American crew to recover electric power from Mir's damaged Spektr module would be manufactured on Sunday and delivered to the Baikonur cosmodrome on Monday.

The cargo craft, which before Wednesday's accident had been due to begin a routine mission on Friday, would be removed from the launch pad temporarily for reloading, he added. Progress craft typically take two days to reach Mir.

Koptev said Mir spent a normal night in orbit after its engines were used to reposition the space station -- Wednesday's collision with another Progress craft had knocked its solar panels out of line with the Sun, depriving it of power. The crew were still attempting other work to hold the craft in position without using up fuel.

The temperature on the station was 23 degrees Centigrade (73 Fahrenheit), five (10) degrees above normal. Humidity was also rather higher but air pressure was normal. The Spektr module was sealed off after being holed in the collision.
